stages.title: Reading and writing fundamentals
stages.hook: Which stroke do you write first in 十: the horizontal or the vertical one? Rules help you write neatly.
explain: Chinese characters are written with strokes (笔画, bǐhuà). A few simple rules guide the order: write from top to bottom, write from left to right, write horizontal before vertical when they cross (十), and write the outside frame of a box before the inside.

Many characters have two parts: a radical (部首, bùshǒu) that often hints at meaning and another part that often hints at sound. In 妈 (mā), the radical 女 means woman and 马 (mǎ) hints at the sound. In 河 (hé, river), 氵 means water.
Pinyin helps you read and type. Learners type pinyin on a keyboard and choose the right character from a list. Reading characters, though, means recognising the shapes, so practise a few every day.
stages.mnemonic: Top to bottom, left to right, cross before close.
sentences: I am learning to write Chinese characters.

gq.q: In 十, which stroke is written first?
gq.why: Horizontal strokes come before vertical ones when they cross.

gq.q: The character 河 (river) has 氵 on the left. What does this radical suggest?
gq.why: 氵 is the water radical, so it hints at water.

panel.q: Why can pinyin typing not replace learning characters completely?
o: Computers cannot display Chinese characters at all, so only pinyin works
Pinyin contains no letters, only tone marks and symbols
You must recognise the characters from a list
Pinyin is a different language, not a way to spell Mandarin sounds
panel.why: To choose the right character you must recognise its shape, since many characters share a pinyin spelling.

panel.q: In 妈 (mā), 女 is the left part and 马 is the right. What does 马 mostly contribute?
o: The meaning 'woman', repeated from the left side
The tone mark, which sits above the vowel
Only the stroke count, with no link to meaning or sound
panel.why: In many characters one part hints at the sound; here 马 (mǎ) is close to mā.

panel.q: Which stroke rule is correct for writing 三?
o: Top line, middle line, bottom line
Bottom line first, then the middle, then the top line
Middle line first, then the top and bottom lines
Any order is fine because all three lines are identical
panel.why: Strokes in a stack are written from top to bottom.

teach.topic: How to write a Chinese character
teach.model: A character is written one stroke at a time. The rules are: top to bottom, left to right, and horizontal before vertical. Many characters have a radical for meaning and another part for sound.

points.ask: What order do I write the strokes?
What does the radical do?
What does the other part do?

trip.prompt: Find the stroke order chart and trace the order of 人 or 大.

stages.title: Basic sentence construction
stages.hook: In English you say "I eat rice". Is the Chinese order the same? Build the sentence block by block.
explain: A basic Mandarin sentence is subject + verb + object: 我吃米饭. The verb 是 (shì) links two nouns: 我是学生 (I am a student). It is used before nouns, but not before simple adjectives: 我很高, not 我是高.

To say "not", put 不 before the verb: 我不是医生 (I am not a doctor). The word 也 (yě) means also and goes before the verb: 她也是老师 (she is also a teacher). 都 (dōu) means all or both and also goes before the verb.
Pronouns have a simple plural: add 们 (men) to 我, 你 and 他/她 to make 我们, 你们 and 他们. The words 他, 她 and 它 sound identical (tā) but are written differently for he, she and it.
stages.mnemonic: Say who, add 不 or 也, then the verb: 我也不是!

gq.q: Where does 也 (also) go in a sentence?
gq.why: Adverbs like 也 and 不 go before the verb.
们 makes a plural; 我们 means we.

panel.q: A learner says 我是高. What is the better sentence?
panel.why: Simple adjectives usually do not need 是; say 我很高.

panel.q: How do you say "They are all students"?
panel.why: 都 means all and goes before 是.

panel.q: Why are 他 and 她 both pronounced tā?
o: They have different tones, so people can hear the difference
Writing shows the difference, speech does not
They are never used together in one text or sentence
One of them is an error and is no longer used
panel.why: Spoken Mandarin has the same sound for both; characters show gender in writing.

teach.model: The basic order is subject, verb, object. To say not use 不 before the verb and to say also use 也 before the verb. You add 们 to make a pronoun plural.

points.ask: What is the order of words?
How do I make a sentence negative?
How do I say we?

trip.prompt: Find the section on word order and compare it with English.

stages.title: Common verbs
stages.hook: Which verb would you use to say "I go to school"? And to say "I want to buy a book"?
explain: Here are common verbs: 去 (qù) go, 来 (lái) come, 学 (xué) study, 买 (mǎi) buy, 做 (zuò) do or make, 想 (xiǎng) want to or think, 要 (yào) want or need, 住 (zhù) live. They do not change form for I, you or he.
The word 想 plus a verb says what you would like to do: 我想买书 means I would like to buy a book. 要 is stronger: it means want or need, and 不要 means do not want or do not.
To show something is completed, add 了 (le) after the verb: 我买了书 means I bought a book. The place word 在 (zài) shows where: 我住在北京 means I live in Beijing.
stages.mnemonic: 去 goes away, 来 comes near; 买 pays money, 学 learns.
sentences: He wants to buy a book.

gq.q: What does 我买了书 mean?
o: I want to buy a book
gq.why: 了 after the verb shows completion.
住 means to live or to stay.

panel.q: What is the difference between 我想去 and 我要去?
o: 想 is a wish and 要 is stronger
想 is past and 要 is future only
There is no difference at all
panel.why: 想 expresses a wish; 要 is stronger, meaning want or need to.

panel.q: How do you say "Come here"?
panel.why: 来 means come; 这儿 means here.

panel.q: Why is the verb 去 the same in 他去 and 我们去?
o: Verbs do not change with person
panel.why: Chinese verbs do not conjugate.

teach.model: Some key verbs are 去 go, 来 come, 学 study, 买 buy, 想 want to and 住 live. They never change form. Put 了 after a verb to show it is done.

points.ask: Which verbs mean go and come?
Do the verbs change form?
How do I show an action is completed?

trip.prompt: Find the page section about aspect particles such as 了.

stages.title: Nouns, pronouns and modifiers
stages.hook: You can say "one book" in English. In Chinese you must add a little counting word. Which one?
explain: Mandarin uses measure words (also called classifiers) between a number or 这/那 and a noun. Common ones are 本 (běn) for books, 只 (zhī) for many animals, 条 (tiáo) for long things such as fish, 杯 (bēi) for cups of drinks, and 个 (gè) for general use.
The particle 的 (de) shows belonging: 我的猫 is my cat. Adjectives can stand before a noun, joined by 的: 红色的书 is a red book. To say "these" or "those" use 这些 and 那些.
Words like 这个 (zhège) this one and 那个 (nàge) that one point at things. 你们 means you (plural) and 他们 means they.
stages.mnemonic: Count with the right helper: books 本, animals 只, long fish 条.

gq.q: Which measure word goes with 书 (book)?
gq.why: 本 is used for books and notebooks.

gq.q: How do you say "a red book"?

panel.q: Why is 一条鱼 correct and 一只鱼 less usual?
o: 条 is for long things like fish
panel.why: 条 is used for long, flexible things such as fish, rivers and roads.

panel.q: What do the measure words add that English does not require?
o: They show the tone of the noun that follows
They mark the past tense of the verb
They replace the noun so it can be left out
panel.why: Mandarin needs a classifier whenever a noun is counted, and it can show the kind of thing.

panel.q: A learner is unsure which measure word to use. What is a safe choice?
panel.why: 个 is the general measure word and can be understood for many nouns.

teach.model: When you count or point with a number, Mandarin adds a measure word. 本 is for books, 只 for many animals and 条 for long things. 个 is the general one. 的 shows possession.

points.ask: What is a measure word?
Can you give some examples?
What does 的 do?

trip.prompt: Find a table of classifiers and list three with their typical nouns.

stages.title: Questions and responses
stages.hook: In English, questions change word order. In Chinese, do you move the words? Let us find out.
explain: The easiest question adds 吗 (ma) to a statement: 你是学生吗？ means are you a student? Answer with the verb: 是 or 不是. Chinese does not use one word for yes. You repeat the verb or use 对 (duì), meaning correct.

For information questions, keep the same word order and put the question word where the answer goes: 你去哪儿？ (nǐ qù nǎr, where do you go?), 这是什么？ (what is this?), 他是谁？ (who is he?). Other words are 几 (jǐ, how many, small numbers), 多少 (duōshao, how much), 为什么 (why) and 怎么 (how).
Do not add 吗 when you already have a question word. 你去哪儿吗？ is wrong. A good reply can be short: 去学校 (going to school).
stages.mnemonic: Same order, swap in the question word: 你去哪儿？

gq.q: Which sentence is a correct yes/no question?
gq.why: Add 吗 to the end of a statement.

gq.q: Where does the question word go in 你去哪儿？
o: At the front of the sentence
gq.why: Question words stay in the same place as the answer would be.

panel.q: Why is 你去哪儿吗？ wrong?
o: 哪儿 is a verb, so it cannot follow 去 in a question
去 cannot be used with place words in questions
It has both a question word and 吗
It needs 的 after the place word to be complete
panel.why: A question word already makes the sentence a question, so 吗 is not added.

panel.q: How might you answer 你是老师吗？ with "yes"?
panel.why: Mandarin repeats the verb: 是, or says 对.

panel.q: Which question asks for a price?
panel.why: 多少钱 asks how much money.

teach.model: For yes/no questions, add 吗 to the end. For other questions put 什么, 谁 or 哪儿 where the answer would go. The word order does not change.

points.ask: How do I make a yes or no question?
And a question with what or where?
Do I move the words around?

trip.prompt: Find the section on interrogative sentences.

stages.title: Describing people and places
stages.hook: How would you describe your friend, your town and your school? Adjectives are easy in Chinese.
explain: Adjectives in Mandarin work like verbs: 她很高 means she is tall (literally she very tall). You usually put 很 (hěn) before an adjective in a simple statement, and you do not need 是. For not, use 不: 她不高.

Useful describing words are 高 (gāo) tall, 矮 (ǎi) short, 漂亮 (piàoliang) pretty, 年轻 (niánqīng) young, 干净 (gānjìng) clean, 热闹 (rènao) lively and 安静 (ānjìng) quiet. 远 (yuǎn) means far, and 近 (jìn) means near.
To say how far apart two places are, use 离 (lí): 学校离我家很近 means the school is close to my home. Describing a place uses the verb 有 as well: 我的城市有一座大公园.
stages.mnemonic: Adjectives are verbs in disguise: 很 + adjective.
sentences: The school is near my home.

gq.q: Which sentence correctly says "He is tall"?
gq.why: Adjectives take 很 and no 是.

gq.q: Which word means the opposite of 远?

panel.q: Why does 她很高 not include 是?
panel.why: Adjectives in Mandarin act like verbs and do not need a linking verb.

panel.q: What does 离 do in 学校离我家很近?
o: It shows distance between two places
It means 'and', joining the school and the home
It means 'go', so the school goes toward home
It turns the sentence into a question about distance
panel.why: 离 means away from and is used for distance between two places.

panel.q: A learner says 这个城市是很热闹. What is better?
panel.why: Use 很 + adjective, without 是.

teach.model: Mandarin adjectives work like verbs. We say 她很高 with 很 and no 是. To show distance use 离, as in 学校离我家很近.

points.ask: What goes before the adjective?
Do I need 是?
How do I talk about distance?

trip.prompt: Find how adjectives behave like verbs in Chinese.

stages.title: Time, dates and daily routines
stages.hook: What is today's date? In Chinese, you start with the biggest unit: year, month, day.
explain: In Mandarin, time goes from big to small. A date is written 年 (year), 月 (month), 日 or 号 (day): 2026年10月12日. Days of the week are 星期一 (Monday) to 星期六 (Saturday) and 星期日 or 星期天 (Sunday).
Time words come before the verb: 我七点起床 means I get up at seven. 点 (diǎn) is o'clock and 分 (fēn) is minute. Common words are 今天 (today), 明天 (tomorrow), 昨天 (yesterday) and 早上 (morning).
A daily routine: 起床 (get up), 吃早饭 (eat breakfast), 上学 (go to school). Because time words come before the verb, say 我今天去学校, not 我去学校今天.
stages.mnemonic: Big to small: year, month, day, hour.

gq.q: How do you write the date 12 October 2026 in Chinese order?
gq.why: The order is year, month, day.

gq.q: Where does a time word like 明天 go?
gq.why: Time words come before the verb, usually after the subject.

panel.q: Which sentence has natural word order?
panel.why: Time words go before the verb.

panel.q: Why does the date start with the year?
panel.why: Chinese orders time from the largest unit to the smallest.

panel.q: How do you say "Monday" in Chinese?
panel.why: 星期 means week; 一 is one, so 星期一 is Monday.

teach.model: Mandarin gives time from big to small, as in year, month, day. Time words usually go before the verb: 我七点起床 means I get up at seven.

points.ask: In what order is a date written?
Where does the time word go?
How do I say a day of the week?

trip.prompt: Find the page on the days of the week and how they are named.

stages.title: Food and shopping
stages.hook: You are at a market. How do you ask for the price and say it is too expensive?
explain: Common foods are 米饭 (mǐfàn, rice), 面条 (miàntiáo, noodles), 水果 (shuǐguǒ, fruit) and 茶 (chá, tea). People say 我想吃 (I would like to eat) or 我想喝 (I would like to drink). In China, tea is very common to drink.

To ask the price, say 多少钱？(duōshao qián?). The spoken word for the unit of money is 块 (kuài), and in writing it is 元 (yuán). The money of China is called 人民币 (rénmínbì). 贵 (guì) means expensive and 便宜 (piányi) means cheap.
To bargain politely at a market, say 太贵了 (too expensive) and 便宜一点吧 (a little cheaper, please). The particle 吧 (ba) softens a request.
stages.mnemonic: Ask 多少钱, say 太贵了, then smile: 便宜一点吧.
sentences: I would like to eat noodles.
Too expensive, a bit cheaper please.

gq.q: Which question asks about the price?
gq.why: 多少钱 asks how much money.

o: It is very cheap, so I will buy it
I would like to buy more of it
gq.why: 太 means too, 贵 means expensive.

panel.q: Why is 吧 added to 便宜一点吧?
o: It makes it a question about where
panel.why: 吧 softens the request, making it more polite.

panel.q: Which pair is correct?
o: 元 spoken only, 块 never used
They are the same as 个
panel.why: 块 is the spoken unit, and 元 is used in writing.

panel.q: A shopkeeper says 十块. What does she mean?
panel.why: 块 is the spoken word for yuan, so ten yuan.

teach.model: To ask the price say 多少钱. 贵 means expensive and 便宜 means cheap. People say 块 for yuan in speech. Adding 吧 makes a request softer.

points.ask: How do I ask the price?
How do I say expensive?
What is the money word?

trip.prompt: Find the name of China's currency and its main unit.

stages.title: Everyday conversations
stages.hook: You meet a friend after a long time. What would you say, and how would they answer?
explain: A typical short conversation: A says 好久不见！你好吗？ (long time no see, how are you?). B says 我很好，你呢？ (I am fine, and you?). 呢 (ne) turns a statement into "and you?" without repeating the whole sentence.

To suggest doing something together, say 一起去吧 (let us go together). To agree, say 好啊 or 没问题 (no problem). To end a conversation politely say 再见 or 慢走, which means walk slowly or take care to the person leaving.
Conversation in Mandarin is also about rhythm and tone. Keep each tone clear, use small words such as 啊 and 吧 to be friendly, and thank people with 谢谢你的帮助 (thank you for your help).
stages.mnemonic: Meet, ask 你好吗, reply 我很好, return with 你呢?
sentences: Long time no see, how are you?

gq.q: What does 你呢？ mean after someone says 我很好?
gq.why: 呢 returns the question: and you?

gq.q: Which reply agrees to a suggestion?
gq.why: 没问题 means no problem and shows agreement.

panel.q: Why is 慢走 said to someone leaving?
o: It tells them to walk slowly because they are slow
It wishes the person a safe trip
It is only used for children
panel.why: It literally means walk slowly, a polite way to wish a safe trip.

panel.q: A friend says 一起去吧. Which is the friendliest response?
panel.why: 好啊 agrees warmly.

panel.q: What does the ending 吧 do in 我们一起去吧?
o: It makes it a past event
panel.why: 吧 suggests or proposes, softening the sentence.

teach.model: You can greet a friend with 你好吗, reply with 我很好 and return the question with 你呢. To suggest going together say 一起去吧, and to agree say 没问题.

points.ask: How do I ask how someone is?
How do I ask it back?
How do I suggest doing something together?

trip.prompt: Listen for a greeting dialogue on the page or in a linked audio sample.
